# Handoff — single canonical product layout (2026-11-18)

## Diagnosis
Product and category HTML pages were being redirected on phone-width viewports by two layers:
- `seo-shell-chrome.mjs` injected an early inline `stm-early` script that hid the document and used `location.replace('/?product=...')` or `/?cat=...`.
- `shell-chrome.js` repeated the phone-width redirect and also handled legacy `?shell=1` links.

The redirect deliberately excluded crawler and speed-test user agents, creating different routing for crawlers and ordinary visitors. This was a redirect architecture issue, not a hydration-only FOUC.

## Changes on branch
- Removed route-changing code from `shell-chrome.js`; it now only adds navigation chrome.
- Disabled new `stm-early` injection and made the generator strip existing legacy early scripts from generated pages.
- Kept the generated product pages, their responsive inline CSS, product content, checkout links, and clean self-referencing canonical tags.
- Added a regression test and made the product-page workflow run it. The workflow now rebuilds generated pages without the legacy inline redirect.

## SEO / CWV notes
- Canonical product URLs remain `https://stermontarcade.co.ke/p/<slug>.html` as generated by `generate-products.mjs`.
- The query-string shell route is no longer used as a redirect destination from product pages.
- Product page content and critical product CSS are already emitted in static HTML; GitHub Pages does not provide native SSR. No SSR migration is required for this fix.
- The navigation chrome is still progressively added by deferred JS. The existing head style reserves the header and mobile purchase/navigation space to reduce layout movement. Confirm actual CLS/LCP/INP with PageSpeed Insights and field data after deployment.

## Release checks still required
- Run `node seo-shell-chrome.test.mjs` and the full `product-pages.yml` workflow.
- Confirm generated `p/*.html` no longer contain `stm-early` or the `location.replace('/?product=...')` redirect.
- Confirm each product has exactly one self-referencing clean canonical URL.
- Verify on a real mobile device and in Search Console after merge/deployment.
